explain.say: As its long orbit brings it near the Sun, the heat turns its ice straight into gas, which bursts out carrying dust. This makes a vast glowing cloud around the nucleus, called the coma, which can be bigger than Earth.

faq.q: What is a comet made of?
faq.a: A comet's solid core, the nucleus, is a mix of water ice, frozen gases like carbon dioxide, dust and rock. Most nuclei are just a few kilometres across.
asks: Is a comet a dirty snowball?

faq.a: The coma is the huge fuzzy cloud of gas and dust around a comet's nucleus, made when sunlight heats the ice. It can grow larger than Earth even though the nucleus is tiny.
asks: Why is a comet's head fuzzy?

faq.q: Why does a comet have two tails?
faq.a: Two different pushes from the Sun. Sunlight gently pushes dust grains into a curved dust tail, while the solar wind blows charged gas into a straight blue ion tail.

faq.q: Which way does a comet's tail point?
faq.a: Always away from the Sun, not simply behind the comet. When a comet is heading away from the Sun, its tails stream out in front of it.
asks: Does a comet's tail trail behind it?

faq.a: Most come from the cold outer Solar System: short-period comets from the Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune, and long-period comets from the distant Oort Cloud. Halley's Comet returns about every 76 years and is next due in 2061.
asks: When will Halley's Comet come back?

facts: A comet's tails always point away from the Sun.
Halley's Comet returns about every 76 years; it last passed near the Sun in 1986 and is due back in 2061.
The European Rosetta spacecraft orbited comet 67P from 2014 to 2016 and landed the Philae probe on it.

quiz.why: Sunlight and the solar wind push the tails directly away from the Sun, whichever way the comet is moving.

wrong.0: The tails are pushed by the Sun, so they never point towards it.
wrong.1: There is no down in space; the tails follow the Sun's push.
